epic.intent:
## Outcome

Agents in terminal sessions and people in the desktop app can attach images (screenshots, mockups, reference images), and the desktop app shows them. Workers attach screenshots as evidence when they submit an attempt. Planners and people attach mockups or reference images to tickets, Kanban cards and comments, so workers have visual references to build from. Today evidence and references are text-only.

## Decisions (from the person)

- **Storage follows the folder's storage mode.** In `db` mode, images are stored as blobs in SQLite. In repository mode, image files sit next to the JSON records that reference them (for example beside the run history or card record holding the evidence), and the record points to the file by path.
- **People can add images from the app** (for example paste or drag-and-drop), as well as agents through the `dm` CLI and MCP tools.
- **Allowed source folders** for images an agent attaches by path: the project folder and its worktrees, the system temp folder, and the OS screenshot folder.
- **Linear is out of scope.** Transfers to Linear do not upload images.

## Scope

- Attach images from the CLI/MCP surface and from the desktop app to attempt evidence (epic and Kanban), and to tickets, Kanban cards and comments as references.
- Store attachments per the storage decision above, so they persist and, in repository mode, travel with the portable state.
- Render images inline in the desktop app: thumbnails that open an enlarged view.
- Label each image as evidence or as a mockup/reference.
- Let workers read attached images back, by path or content, while they implement.
- Enforce size and type limits (PNG and JPEG; no SVG).

## Findings from the codebase survey

- No binary storage exists. `FsAdapter` reads and writes text only and needs binary read, write and hash methods. Records cap at 8 MiB (`run.json` holds every attempt of a run) and comments at 256 KiB, so images are never inlined as base64.
- Attempt evidence (`checks`, `criteria`, `notes`) has no attachment field. A new ticket field must be optional with no default so saved plan content hashes do not change.
- Image files must be written before the record that points to them (the snapshot-before-pointer rule in `finalizer.ts`). The importers need to scan and verify attachments with containment, size and count limits; a missing file shows as missing rather than failing the import.
- A new outbox record kind means rebuilding the `outbox` and `sync_state` tables, as v13 did.
- The CLI takes its JSON as one positional argument (no stdin, no input file), and Windows caps a command line at about 32K characters, so images are passed by file path, with an `attach` subcommand or an `--input-file` option.
- The renderer has no custom protocol, and in dev the page is served over http and cannot load `file:` images. Serve attachments through a dedicated protocol (or bytes over IPC) by attachment id only; the renderer never handles paths (`src/shared/desktop/api.ts`). Images inside untrusted Markdown stay disabled.
- References, ticket `expectedArtifacts` and `outputs.artifacts` are not shown in the ticket or attempt views today; this epic displays them.
- Role guides (worker, reviewer, planner, sprint-reporter), chat kickoff text and the CLI runbook need updating.

## Risks

- Reading paths an agent supplies could copy secrets into committed records. Restrict sources, refuse links, check the file type by its contents, and cap size and dimensions.
- Images committed with `.darkmechanicus` grow the repository; show attachment bytes in storage status.

## Standards

Only the project's Definition of Done. No tests-first and no Fireguard in this epic. Each ticket's **Tests** section lists the tests its worker writes and runs.

## Out of scope

- Uploading images to Linear.
- Image editing or annotation in the app.
- Video or other binary attachment types.

## Origin

Started as Kanban card DM-420, which was too large for one card. DM-420 now tracks deleting Kanban cards from the app.

bundle.rationale:
Assumptions:
- The SQLite database holds attachment bytes in both storage modes and the app serves from it; in repo mode files are also exported next to the owning record (the person's decision: blobs in SQL for database-only folders, files next to JSON otherwise). Keeping bytes in SQLite in repo mode is my choice: it mirrors how other records work (database first, files exported) and lets the app serve one way.
- Agents attach by local file path because the CLI takes JSON as one argument and Windows caps command lines near 32K characters. The desktop app uploads bytes instead, so no path crosses the renderer bridge.
- Allowed folders: project and worktrees, system temp, OS screenshot folder (the person's decision).
- Limits (10 MiB, 8,000 px, 20 per record, PNG and JPEG only) are my defaults; change them before Save if you want others.
- Linear transfers do not carry images (the person's decision).

Graph:
- Sprint 1: intake and storage start in parallel; commands joins them; portable export follows storage; evidence joins commands and portable; the protocol and gallery follow storage; the evidence UI joins evidence and protocol. Critical path: store → portable → evidence → evidenceUi.
- Sprint 2: comments, card references, ticket references and storage status run in parallel; app upload joins the three reference tickets; docs follow app upload.

tickets.body:
## Context
Agents attach images by local file path (the CLI takes its JSON as one argument, and Windows caps a command line near 32K characters, so bytes cannot be passed inline). Reading a path an agent supplies could copy secrets into committed records, so intake is restricted.

## Attachment model (shared by this epic)
- An attachment is one image: stable id (new id kind `attachment`; pick an unused prefix such as `at` and register it wherever stable id kinds are listed), `sha256`, `mime` (`image/png` or `image/jpeg`), `bytes`, `width`, `height`, `label`, `purpose` (`evidence` or `reference`), `owner` (`{kind: 'attempt' | 'kanban_attempt' | 'comment' | 'kanban_card' | 'ticket', id}`, or null while staged), `createdBy` (session role and label), `createdAt`.
- Records reference images with an `attachmentRef`: `{id, sha256, mime, bytes, width, height, label, purpose}`. Never base64 inside a record.
- SQLite always holds the metadata and the bytes (BLOB) in both storage modes; the app serves from it. In `repo` mode the bytes are also exported as files next to the record that owns them: `history/<runId>/attachments/<sha256>.<ext>` (epic attempt evidence), `kanban/<cardId>/attachments/<sha256>.<ext>` (card references and card attempt evidence), `epics/<epicId>/attachments/<sha256>.<ext>` (comments and ticket references). In `db` mode no files are written.
- Limits: PNG and JPEG only, detected by magic bytes; at most 10 MiB per file and 8,000 px per side; at most 20 attachments per record. SVG is always refused.
- Allowed source folders for agent paths: the project root and its worktrees, the system temp folder, and the OS screenshot folder.

## Do
Create `src/core/attachments/intake.ts` (pure Node, no Electron) exporting:
- `resolveAllowedRoots({repoRoot, worktrees, env, platform, homeDir})`: the project root, its git worktrees, `os.tmpdir()`, and the OS screenshot folder (Windows `%USERPROFILE%\Pictures\Screenshots`, plus the OneDrive Pictures\Screenshots folder when `OneDrive` is set; macOS the `com.apple.screencapture location` default when readable, else `~/Desktop`; Linux `$XDG_PICTURES_DIR/Screenshots` or `~/Pictures/Screenshots`). Missing folders are skipped. Inject env and platform so tests do not depend on the machine.
- `readImageFile(path, roots, fs)`: realpath the file and each root; refuse when the file is not inside a root, is a symbolic link, or is not a regular file; read the bytes; return `{bytes, sha256, mime, width, height}`.
- `inspectImageBytes(bytes)`: shared with the desktop upload later. Detect PNG/JPEG by magic bytes (ignore the extension), parse width and height from the PNG IHDR or JPEG SOF marker without a new dependency, and enforce the limits above.
- Failures throw a DomainError with code `invalid_input` and a message naming the reason (outside allowed folders, link, unsupported type, too large, too many pixels).

Out of scope: storage, commands, UI.

## Tests
`src/core/attachments/intake.test.ts`: accepts a PNG and a JPEG in the project root and in the temp folder; refuses a file outside every root, a symlink into a root, an SVG, a text file renamed .png, an over-size file and an over-dimension header; a PNG renamed .jpg is accepted as PNG; resolveAllowedRoots for win32, darwin and linux with injected env.

reasoning.rationale: Security boundary on reading agent-supplied paths; a wrong call leaks secrets into committed records.

reasoning.rationale: Schema migration with a table rebuild plus a new service; must keep existing rows.

- `getAttachment` with `as: 'file'` writes the bytes to `<os tmpdir>/darkmechanicus-attachments/<sha256>.<ext>` (reuse when present) and returns its absolute path, so a worker can open a mockup; `metadata` returns the view only.
- MCP: register `add_attachment` and `get_attachment` in a new `src/mcp/tools/attachments.ts` via `defineTool`.
- CLI: `--describe` and `--list` pick them up from the registry; confirm `dm call add_attachment` works with Windows paths written with forward slashes or escaped backslashes.

In `db` mode no files are written.
- Limits: PNG and JPEG only, detected by magic bytes; at most 10 MiB per file and 8,000 px per side; at most 20 attachments per record. SVG is always refused.
- Allowed source folders for agent paths: the project root and its worktrees, the system temp folder, and the OS screenshot folder.
The file layer is text-only today (`FsAdapter` in `src/core/repo/types.ts`; `nodeFs.ts` uses utf8). Records are written by outbox handlers in `src/core/repo/finalizer.ts`; images must be written before the record that points at them (the snapshot-before-pointer rule, ~470-478).

## Do
- `FsAdapter`: add `readFileBytes(path): Uint8Array` and `writeFileBytes(path, data: Uint8Array)`; implement them in `nodeFs.ts` and every test fake.
- `src/core/repo/paths.ts` `ownedPaths`: `attachmentFile(owner, sha256, mime)` for the three locations above, built only from validated ids and a hex sha256.
- `finalizer.ts`: an `attachment` outbox handler that writes the file once (temp, fsync, rename, read back and compare sha256). Enqueue it whenever an attachment is claimed by an owner, ordered before the owning record's export. `DB_HANDLERS` (db mode) treat it as done without writing.
- Importers (`importer.ts`, `kanbanImport.ts`): read `attachments/` folders inside run, card and epic folders; verify the hash and the image type; enforce containment (`assertContained`), at most 2,000 files and 512 MiB per folder; store bytes in the attachments table. A record that references a missing or corrupt file imports with the attachment flagged missing instead of failing.
- Epic and card removal already delete their folders; confirm attachments go with them.

## Tests
- `finalizer.test.ts`: the attachment file is written before the record that references it, and db mode writes nothing.
- Importer tests: export then import restores byte-identical attachments; a missing file imports as missing; a file with a wrong hash is refused; a symlink in attachments/ is refused.

reasoning.rationale: Write ordering and import verification in the sync layer; mistakes corrupt state across machines.

The renderer is sandboxed and must never receive or send file paths (`src/shared/desktop/api.ts` ~68-71). There is no custom protocol yet, and the dev page is served from http://localhost, which cannot load `file:` images. The CSP (`electron.vite.config.ts` ~8-26) allows `img-src 'self' data: file:`.

## Do
- `src/main`: register `dm-attachment` as a privileged standard, secure scheme before app ready, and `protocol.handle` it: `dm-attachment://<folder handle>/<attachmentId>`, where the folder handle is the identifier the renderer already passes to `dm:command` (never a path). Look the id up through the workspace and respond with the stored bytes, the stored mime, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable`; 404 for unknown ids or ids flagged missing; GET only.
- CSP: replace `file:` with `dm-attachment:` in `img-src` for both prod and dev policies.
- Renderer: `src/renderer/src/attachments/AttachmentGallery.tsx`: thumbnails (fixed height, label and an Evidence/Reference badge); click opens a lightbox at full size, with Escape and arrow keys; a missing attachment shows a placeholder with its label. Use existing theme tokens and components.
- Markdown keeps refusing images.

## Tests
- Main: unit test of the request handler (known id returns bytes and headers; unknown returns 404; non-GET returns 405) with a fake workspace.
- Renderer: AttachmentGallery component test for thumbnails, lightbox open and close, and the missing placeholder.
- Verify in the dev app that a stored attachment renders (screenshot).

reasoning.rationale: New Electron protocol and CSP change plus a themed React component checked visually.

## Context
## Attachment model (shared by this epic)
- An attachment is one image: stable id (new id kind `attachment`; pick an unused prefix such as `at` and register it wherever stable id kinds are listed), `sha256`, `mime` (`image/png` or `image/jpeg`), `bytes`, `width`, `height`, `label`, `purpose` (`evidence` or `reference`), `owner` (`{kind: 'attempt' | 'kanban_attempt' | 'comment' | 'kanban_card' | 'ticket', id}`, or null while staged), `createdBy` (session role and label), `createdAt`.
- Records reference images with an `attachmentRef`: `{id, sha256, mime, bytes, width, height, label, purpose}`. Never base64 inside a record.
- SQLite always holds the metadata and the bytes (BLOB) in both storage modes; the app serves from it. In `repo` mode the bytes are also exported as files next to the record that owns them: `history/<runId>/attachments/<sha256>.<ext>` (epic attempt evidence), `kanban/<cardId>/attachments/<sha256>.<ext>` (card references and card attempt evidence), `epics/<epicId>/attachments/<sha256>.<ext>` (comments and ticket references). In `db` mode no files are written.
- Limits: PNG and JPEG only, detected by magic bytes; at most 10 MiB per file and 8,000 px per side; at most 20 attachments per record. SVG is always refused.
- Allowed source folders for agent paths: the project root and its worktrees, the system temp folder, and the OS screenshot folder.

## Do
- `addComment` input (`src/core/commandSchemas.ts` ~131) and `src/core/services/comments.ts` (~114): optional `attachments: string[]` (ids, at most 20); claim them for the comment.
- Comment portable record (`commentRecord` in `src/core/repo/portable.ts` ~424) gets an optional `attachments` array of refs; files export to `epics/<epicId>/attachments/` via the attachment outbox handler. The 256 KiB comment record limit is unaffected since only refs are stored.
- Comment import (`importer.ts`) reads the refs.
- `CommentView` includes refs; `src/renderer/src/ticket/CommentsTab.tsx` (~70) renders them with `AttachmentGallery` under the comment body.

## Tests
- Comments service test: add with staged ids claims them and returns refs; an owned id is refused.
- Portable test: a comment record without attachments parses; one with them round-trips.
- CommentsTab component test renders the gallery.

- Wire it into the comment composer (`CommentsTab.tsx`), the Kanban card form (`kanban/CardFormDialog.tsx`) and the ticket editor (`ticket/TicketEditor.tsx` and `editorFields.tsx`); on save pass the ids through the existing add_comment, create/update card and draft ticket edits.

## Tests
- Command test: desktop transport accepts a PNG; cli transport refused; non-image and oversize refused.
- Hook test: paste and drop produce uploads; an upload error is shown and the image is not attached.
